groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

The sports hall hummed with tension. The final minutes of the inter-school floorball championships ticked away. Wei Han faced a __(16: formidable)__ defense from the opposing team, who had remained undefeated all season. He had __(17: conscientiously)__ practised his shots every afternoon under the scorching sun at the school's floorball court. Despite his aching limbs, Wei Han's __(18: resilience)__ kept him sprinting towards the goal.
With seconds left, he __(19: noticed)__ the goalkeeper leaning slightly to the left. He made a shrewd move, pretending he was __(20: going for)__ a high shot before sliding the ball into the opposite corner. Wei Han felt elated as the whistle blew and his teammates swarmed around him in jubilant celebration. It was a victory that proved determination was the key to success.

Study the poster for a school bag (Text 1) and the extract taken from an online article (Text 2) and answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below shows an advertisement for a bag.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from an online article.
School bags are designed to be both roomy and trendy, which makes them appealing to students. Lately, more focus has been put on making school bags look good. For many students, their school bag is also a way to express their personality and personal style. Is that true for you, too?
While it may seem convenient to fit everything into one bag, have you considered the weight? Carrying too many items strains your back. This may cause short-term discomfort and lead to long-term posture problems. To cushion the effect, you should carry a school bag that fits comfortably on your back. Features such as wide straps and padded backs help distribute weight more evenly. By choosing a school bag wisely, you can reduce the pressure on your back.
Ultimately, health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day to keep your school bag light. For example, store certain items in your school locker or keep some materials under your desk if your school allows it. By planning what you bring each day and leaving out unnecessary items, you can protect your back and still have everything you need.

images.alt: Advertisement. Heading: Peaks School Bag. Carry Everything in Style. Say goodbye to boring school bags. Fit your entire school day into one bag: all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more! Get organised with a specific space for everything. No more mess or things left behind! In the middle is a picture of a backpack with a front pocket and side pockets. On its left: Suitable for students of all ages! On its right: Wide range of colours to choose from! Below: Designed with students in mind! At the bottom, beside a picture of a smiling boy in school uniform carrying a backpack: "I love my Peaks school bag! Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it. I can also find and take out any item I need easily!" – Ansel, primary school student

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

Every day, we enjoy fruits without realising how many quiet changes have taken place inside them. The mystery behind fruit ripening __(26)__ still not fully understood by scientists and farmers. Most fruits are picked when they are still firm and green, as they bruise easily __(27)__ left to ripen fully on the tree. The flesh of these fruits __(28)__ been known to contain a gas called ethylene which acts as a signal to begin __(29)__ ripening process. Ethylene spreads through the cells and reaches the parts __(30)__ the seeds develop. As the level of ethylene rises, the fruit softens, turns sweeter and changes colour.
In storage rooms, workers __(31)__ slow down the ripening process __(32)__ keeping fruits cool and reducing the amount of ethylene in the air. Later, to speed up the ripening process, they may place unripe fruits into closed boxes with a few ripe bananas __(33)__ have already released a lot of ethylene. Similarly, people sometimes put __(34)__ unripe mango in a paper bag with a ripe banana because this simple trick speeds up the ripening process. Scientists are still studying the process of fruit ripening in the hope __(35)__ using this knowledge to reduce food waste and to keep fruit fresh for a longer period.
The next time you watch a hard, green fruit slowly turn soft and sweet, you are witnessing this hidden ripening process at work.

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

It was Jia Wei's first day back in school. He had already regretted __(36: volentiering)__ for the student council project. He and three classmates were tasked __(37: by)__ planning an exhibition on Singapore's __(38: enviromantle)__ efforts. The principal had also made it clear that everyone __(39: are)__ expecting something impressive. As Jia Wei __(40: skrold)__ through old photographs of the Singapore harbour, he noticed a photograph of a coastline that looked nothing like the present one. The caption said it was taken before land reclamation had __(41: begin)__ in the area. He felt a sudden urge to find out what the town might lose if people only cared about __(42: sprauling)__ shopping malls and new MRT lines. __(43: Althought)__, his friends were far more interested in designing beautiful posters instead of checking their facts. After a long discussion, the group still had no clear __(44: konsept)__. Walking home, Jia Wei realised __(45: what)__ easily a city's memories could disappear beneath glass and concrete. The thought stayed with him long after he reached home.

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

Zubir Said was the composer who wrote "Majulah Singapura", the national anthem of Singapore. Born in 1907 in Sumatra, Zubir grew up in a poor household where money was always __(46)__ enough but music was always present. __(47)__ a teenager, he left home and sailed to Singapore. His __(48)__ from childhood was to become a professional musician. The first __(49)__ he had was playing the violin and piano in silent movie theatres, bringing the film to __(50)__ with his music. The work was tiring and the pay was low, but these early experiences honed his skills and confidence as a composer.
In 1958, the City Council of Singapore invited him to __(51)__ a special song for a civic celebration. He __(52)__ the task readily. He walked along crowded streets and quiet kampungs, hoping __(53)__ would inspire him to write the perfect song. He __(54)__ the song to capture the aspirations of a young nation – its courage, unity and hope. After many revisions, he composed a clear and rousing __(55)__ that ordinary people could remember and sing with pride. The song impressed the leaders, and it was later __(56)__ as the national anthem of Singapore.
Although he __(57)__ studied at prestigious music schools, Zubir kept improving his musical technique by listening carefully to other composers and reflecting on his own work. He believed that a national anthem __(58)__ not only sound grand but also encourage citizens to serve their country and care for one another.
Today, students in school sing "Majulah Singapura" during assemblies and national __(59)__ like the Primary 5 National Education (NE) Show so that they are __(60)__ of the sacrifices and dreams that helped build Singapore. His story continues to spur young people to contribute in their own ways to the nation.

Read the passage and answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** Maya had always admired her grandfather's magnificent vegetable garden, which was truly the apple of his eye. It stretched across the entire back corner of their family property. Every morning at precisely six o'clock, she watched him tend to his prized tomatoes, crisp lettuce, and fragrant herbs with meticulous care, treating each plant with the gentle attention of a devoted parent nurturing his child. When her grandfather fell ill and had to stay in hospital for two weeks, Maya's heart sank as she saw her dear grandfather's plants beginning to wilt under the relentless scorching sun.
**2** "Mum, can I take care of Grandpa's garden while he's away?" Maya asked earnestly, her voice trembling with emotion. Her mother gave her a concerned look. "Are you sure you want to do it? This would be a big responsibility, Maya. Plants need daily attention, you know? It'll be an uphill task for you."
**3** The next morning, Maya woke up early and rushed eagerly to the garden with nervous excitement fluttering wildly in her stomach like trapped butterflies. Although she had watched her grandfather's practised movements countless times, doing it herself the first time felt like an arduous task. The metal watering can was heavier than expected, and she was not sure how much water each plant actually needed. After soaking the thirsty plants thoroughly, she noticed the lettuce leaves looked droopy despite her efforts, making her feel deeply worried.
**4** Feeling extremely discouraged, Maya called her best friend, Sandie, for advice. "My grandmother grows vegetables too! Let me ask her for her opinion and I will call you back immediately," Sandie offered without hesitation. Within an hour, Sandie arrived breathlessly with her elderly grandmother, Mrs Chen, who began to examine the struggling garden with the sharp, keen eye of an experienced gardener.
**5** "You're doing remarkably well, dear, but different plants need different amount of water," Mrs Chen explained patiently. "For example, the soil for lettuce should not be too wet," Mrs Chen said. "Gardening requires patience. **Rome wasn't built in a day, and neither is a beautiful garden.**"
**6** Over the next few days, Maya took Sandie's grandmother's advice to heart, taking special care not to overwater the plants, especially the lettuce. Sandie often joined her, and together, they removed stubborn weeds and dead leaves, making the demanding work considerably easier and much more enjoyable. Sandie discovered that the aromatic herbs grew noticeably faster after they talked to them, though Maya suspected **it** was just a coincidence.
**7** When some destructive aphids suddenly attacked the vulnerable lettuce plants, Maya's heart raced frantically. However, she refused to give up. Instead, she researched effective natural remedies online and prepared a soap solution which she sprinkled onto the affected leaves. She felt immensely proud watching the tiny green invaders disappear completely after her **treatment**. The garden slowly transformed from wilting to thriving under her dedicated care, flourishing beautifully once again.
**8** Two weeks later, Maya's grandfather returned home to find his garden more beautiful than ever, a truly wonderful sight after his hospital stay. Tears of joy streamed down his cheeks as he saw the healthy plants and Maya's detailed notebook filled with careful observations. "You've done **something wonderful** here," he said, pointing at the plot of land.
**9** "Sandie helped me a lot, and Mrs Chen taught us so much," Maya replied modestly, her cheeks glowing with pride. "I never knew gardening required such dedication. It really taught me a lot."
**10** Her grandfather smiled knowingly, his eyes sparkling with happiness. "The best gardens grow from love and commitment, not just water and sunshine. Would you like to be my gardening partner from now on?" Maya's face lit up with pure joy as she nodded enthusiastically. Her mother nodded and gave her a thumbs-up.

questions.stem: "They've never been to the theatres in Singapore, __________?" Aunt Mona asked.

explanation: Rule: the question tag uses the helping verb of the statement. 'They've' is short for 'They **have**', so the tag uses 'have', not 'did'.
Rule: a positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag.
'never' makes the statement negative, even though there is no 'not'. So the tag must be positive: 'have they'.
'haven't they' is tempting because the verb 'have' looks positive, but 'never' already carries the 'not'. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: The detective was __________ the verge of giving up when he discovered the hidden clue in a dusty diary.

explanation: 'on the verge of' is a fixed phrase. It means very close to doing something.
For example: 'She was on the verge of tears.'
A 'verge' is an edge, and we stand **on** an edge, which helps to remember the preposition.
'The detective was on the verge of giving up...' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: When the old man dropped his groceries, several kind strangers helped him __________ them up from the pavement.

explanation: Rule: help + person + base form of the verb (or 'to' + base form). Example: 'She helped me carry the bags.'
'helped' already shows the past tense, so the second verb is not put into the past again.
'picked' is tempting because the event is in the past, but 'helped him picked' is wrong.
'...several kind strangers helped him pick them up...' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: By the time the school bell rang, all the students __________ their art projects and placed them on display.

explanation: There are two past actions: the bell rang, and the students finished their projects. 'By the time' tells us the finishing happened first.
Rule: for the earlier of two past actions, use the past perfect: had + past participle.
'had finished ... and (had) placed' fits. 'have finished' is present perfect and cannot go with the past 'rang'.
'finished' is tempting, but 'By the time' signals that one action was already complete before the other. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: __________ the noise from the construction work nearby, the children managed to concentrate on their lessons.

explanation: Look at how the two halves are linked: there was noise, yet the children still managed to concentrate. That is a contrast, something unexpected.
'In spite of' + noun shows that something happened even though there was an obstacle.
'Owing to' and 'As a result of' both give a cause, but noise does not cause concentration.
'Contrary to' means 'opposite to what was said or believed' (contrary to popular belief), which does not fit. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Even though he practised for weeks before the school concert, Marcus still had __________ confidence when he walked onto the stage to perform his solo.

explanation: 'Even though' and 'still' signal a surprise: he practised a lot, but the result was not what we expect. So he had almost no confidence.
'confidence' is an uncountable noun. 'little' goes with uncountable nouns and means 'almost no'.
'few' has the same meaning but is used only with countable plural nouns (few friends).
'some' and 'much' would mean he was confident, which is no surprise after weeks of practice. The answer is option (2).

review.note: The question number 6 is missing from the scan (the left margin is cut off); it is the first question on the page, between 5 and 7.

questions.stem: Emma giggled softly when she saw her grandfather alone in the garden, talking to __________ while watering the flowers.

explanation: Who was talking? Her grandfather. He was 'alone', so the only person he could be talking to was himself.
Rule: when the doer and the receiver of an action are the same person, use a reflexive pronoun (-self).
Grandfather is male, so the pronoun is 'himself', not 'herself'.
'her' is tempting because Emma is nearby, but he was alone and did not know she was watching. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Jenna could not stop __________ when she saw her little brother trying to pull his hand out of the cookie jar.

explanation: Rule: stop + verb-ing means to end an action that is going on. 'She could not stop laughing' means the laughing went on and on.
'stop to laugh' has a different meaning: to pause what you are doing in order to laugh. That does not fit 'could not stop'.
'laugh' (base form) cannot follow 'stop' directly.
'Jenna could not stop laughing...' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Among all the books in the library, this mystery novel is definitely __________ one I have ever read.

explanation: Clues: 'Among all the books' and 'I have ever read'. One book is being compared with many others, so we need the superlative.
Rule: the superlative of a long adjective is 'the most' + adjective: the most exciting.
'the more exciting' is the comparative, used when comparing only two things.
'...this mystery novel is definitely the most exciting one I have ever read.' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: "Where __________ the pair of glasses that I placed on the desk this morning?" wondered Mrs Lim.

explanation: Find the subject: 'the pair of glasses'. The head word is 'pair', which is singular, so the verb is singular. That rules out 'are' and 'were'.
Tense: Mrs Lim is looking for the glasses now, so the question is in the present tense: 'Where is...?'
'was' is tempting because of 'placed' and 'this morning', but those describe when she put them down, not when she is asking.
'Where is the pair of glasses...?' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: A fight __________ on the football field when two students started quarrelling over the football.

explanation: Clue: the fight started when the two students began quarrelling.
'break out' means to start suddenly. It is used for fights, fires, wars and diseases.
'broke up' is tempting because we say a teacher 'broke up the fight', but that means stopped it. 'broke off' means stopped suddenly or snapped off, and 'broke down' means stopped working.
The answer is option (3), broke out.

questions.stem: After months of practice, Maria became __________ playing the piano and could perform complex pieces without making mistakes.

explanation: Clues: 'After months of practice' and 'could perform complex pieces without making mistakes'. She became very good at it.
'proficient at' means skilled at something through practice.
'familiar with' is tempting, but it only means knowing something fairly well, not being skilled at it. 'certified in' means holding a certificate, which practice alone does not give.
The answer is option (3), proficient at.

questions.stem: Sarah looked __________ at the tall diving board, worried about jumping into the deep water for the first time.

explanation: Clue: she was 'worried about jumping into the deep water for the first time'.
'apprehensively' means in a worried or nervous way about something that is going to happen.
'quizzically' means in a puzzled, questioning way. 'reproachfully' means in a way that shows blame, and 'cynically' means in a distrusting way.
The answer is option (4), apprehensively.

questions.stem: The firefighters worked hard on the __________ of the wildfire to stop it from spreading to nearby homes.

explanation: Clue: the firefighters wanted 'to stop it from spreading'. They were fighting to put the fire down.
'suppression' means stopping something by force. 'Fire suppression' is the usual term for putting out or holding back a fire.
'reduction' is tempting, but it only means making something smaller, and it is not the word used for fighting fires. 'restriction' is a rule that limits, and 'omission' means leaving something out.
The answer is option (4), suppression.

questions.stem: The storm began to __________ as the wind grew stronger and the rain became heavier throughout the afternoon.

explanation: Clue: 'the wind grew stronger and the rain became heavier'. The storm was getting stronger.
'intensify' means to become stronger or more extreme.
'accelerate' is tempting, but it means to go faster, and the clue is about strength, not speed. 'maximise' needs an object (maximise something), and 'progress' only means to move forward.
The answer is option (1), intensify.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++formidable++.

explanation: 'formidable' describes something so strong or difficult that it is hard to deal with.
Clue in the passage: the opposing team 'had remained undefeated all season', so their defence was very hard to beat.
'tough' means strong and difficult to get past, so it is the closest.
'frightening' is tempting because a formidable opponent can seem scary, but the point here is that the defence was hard to beat, not that Wei Han was afraid. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++conscientiously++.

explanation: 'conscientiously' means carefully and with great effort, because you want to do something well.
Clue: he practised 'every afternoon under the scorching sun', which shows steady hard work.
'diligently' means in a hard-working and careful way, so it matches.
'precisely' means exactly, 'frantically' means in a rushed, panicky way, and 'haphazardly' (without any plan) is the opposite. The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++resilience++.

explanation: 'resilience' is the ability to keep going and bounce back when things are hard.
Clue: 'Despite his aching limbs', it 'kept him sprinting'. He refused to give up even though he was in pain.
'persistence' means continuing to try in spite of difficulty, so it is the closest. The last sentence agrees: 'determination was the key to success'.

'stamina' is tempting, but it is physical energy to keep going, and his limbs were already aching; what kept him going was his will. 'resistance' looks similar but means fighting against something. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++noticed++.

explanation: 'noticed' means saw something and became aware of it.
'observed' means saw or noticed, so it can replace the word directly: 'he observed the goalkeeper leaning slightly to the left'.
'glimpsed' is tempting because it happened quickly, but a glimpse is a very short, incomplete look. 'spied' suggests watching secretly.
'detected' is used for finding something hidden or hard to sense (detect a smell, detect a fault). The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++going for++.

explanation: To 'go for' a shot is to try to make it, to carry it out.
'executing' means carrying out a planned move. 'Pretending he was executing a high shot' keeps the meaning: he acted as if he was making a high shot, then slid the ball low instead.
'pursuing' is tempting because 'go for' can mean 'chase after' (go for gold), but you do not chase a shot. We say 'strike a ball', not 'strike a shot'.
'launching' is close, but it means sending something off, while 'going for' is about attempting the move. The answer is option (3).

review.note: 'launching' (4) is a near miss here; the key gives (3) executing, which was also the solved answer. A parent may want to talk through why 'executing a shot' is the better fit.

questions.stem: The purpose of the statement "Carry Everything in Style" in Text 1 is to __________.
options: highlight that the bag is useful and trendy
command students to care about how they look
remind students about what they must bring to school

explanation: Split the slogan into its two ideas.
'Carry Everything' says the bag can hold all you need, so it is useful. 'in Style' says it looks good, so it is trendy.
Option (2) covers both ideas. Option (1) is tempting but covers only 'Carry Everything' and leaves out 'in Style'.
The slogan is not an order about looks, and it does not list what to bring. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Ansel was quoted in Text 1 because __________.
options: he appears to be a good student
all school bag users are around his age
his review was short enough to fit into the poster
what he said supports the claims made in the poster

explanation: Compare what Ansel says with what the advertisement says.

Advertisement: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag' and 'a specific space for everything'. Ansel: 'Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it. I can also find and take out any item I need easily!'
His words repeat the advertisement's claims in a real user's voice, which makes readers trust them. Advertisers use such quotes (testimonials) for this reason.
(2) is false because the bag is 'Suitable for students of all ages'. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem:
Based on Text 1, which of the following statements are true about the Peaks school bag?
A: The bag is small and light.
B: The bag comes in different colours.
C: The bag has multiple compartments.
D: The bag is only suitable for primary school students.

explanation: Check each statement against the advertisement.
B is true: 'Wide range of colours to choose from!' C is true: 'Get organised with a specific space for everything', which means the bag has many separate sections.
A is not supported: the bag fits 'your entire school day', so it is roomy, and nothing says it is light. D is false: it is 'Suitable for students of all ages!'
The true statements are B and C. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: What is the **main** message of Text 2?
options: Students should take measures to protect their backs.
Students should choose school bags with more features.
Students should express their personality and personal style.
Students should use lockers or desks to store their belongings.

explanation: The main message is the idea that the whole text builds up to, not one detail.
Paragraph 2 warns that 'Carrying too many items strains your back'. Paragraph 3 ends with 'you can protect your back and still have everything you need'.
Choosing a bag with wide straps, packing light and using a locker are all ways to do one thing: protect your back. That is option (1).
Option (4) is tempting, but it is only one example ('For example, store certain items in your school locker'). The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Text 1 and Text 2 express differing views on whether __________.
options: students can store certain items in school
school bags should look appealing to students
school bags can fit everything needed for school
students should fit everything into their school bags

explanation: Look for a point on which the two texts disagree.
Text 1 encourages it: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag: all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more!'
Text 2 advises against it: 'While it may seem convenient to fit everything into one bag, have you considered the weight?' and 'health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day'.
Option (3) is tempting, but Text 2 never says a bag cannot hold everything; it says you **should** not carry everything. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The subject is 'The mystery behind fruit ripening'. The head word is 'mystery', which is singular.
After the blank is 'still not fully understood by scientists'. The mystery does not understand anything; it is understood by people. That is the passive voice: be + past participle.
'still' tells us this is true now, so we need the present tense 'is', not 'was'.
The answer is (J) is.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence gives a condition: fruits bruise easily in one situation, namely when they are left to ripen fully on the tree.
'if left to ripen' is a short form of 'if they are left to ripen'.
The connector for a condition is 'if'.
The answer is (G) if.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank is 'been known', so we need has/have to make the present perfect passive.
Find the subject: 'The flesh of these fruits'. The head word is 'flesh', which is singular. 'of these fruits' only describes it.
A singular subject takes 'has'. 'have' is tempting because 'fruits' is right next to the blank.
The answer is (E) has.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank comes before the noun phrase 'ripening process', so it needs an article or determiner.
The passage has already been talking about fruit ripening, so the reader knows which process is meant. For something specific and already known, use 'the'.
'this' is tempting, but it is needed later, and 'the ripening process' is the phrase the passage repeats.
The answer is (L) the.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The words after the blank ('the seeds develop') describe 'the parts'.
The parts are a place inside the fruit. To add information about a place, use 'where'.
'which' is tempting, but it would need a preposition: 'the parts in which the seeds develop'.
The answer is (P) where.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank is between the subject 'workers' and the base verb 'slow'. A helping verb fits here.
'can' + base verb shows that the workers are able to do this.
No other helping verb in the list works: 'has' and 'have' need a past participle (slowed), and 'is' and 'was' do not fit a base verb.
The answer is (D) can.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The words after the blank say how the workers slow down ripening: 'keeping fruits cool and reducing the amount of ethylene'.
Rule: by + verb-ing tells us the method used to do something.
For example: 'She saved money by walking to school.'
The answer is (C) by.

review.note: In the scan the word bank is damaged: the word beside (B) is only partly printed and the word beside (C) is missing. They are filled in as 'an' and 'by', the only words that fit blanks (34) and (32), and this matches the key's letters (B for 34, C for 32).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The words after the blank ('have already released a lot of ethylene') describe 'a few ripe bananas'.
Bananas are things, so the relative pronoun is 'which'. ('who' is for people.)
The verb 'have' is plural because it agrees with 'bananas'.
The answer is (Q) which.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank comes before 'unripe mango', one mango that has not been mentioned before, so we need 'a' or 'an'.
'unripe' begins with a vowel sound, so the article is 'an'.
'a' is used before consonant sounds (a ripe banana).
The answer is (B) an.

review.note: In the scan the word bank is damaged: the word beside (B) is only partly printed and the word beside (C) is missing. They are filled in as 'an' and 'by', the only words that fit blanks (34) and (32), and this matches the key's letters (B for 34, C for 32).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'in the hope of' is a fixed phrase. It means wishing that something will happen.
It is followed by a verb-ing: 'in the hope of using this knowledge'.
The answer is (K) of.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++volentiering++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means offering to do something without being forced.
Start from the base word 'volunteer': vol-un-teer. The middle is 'un', and the ending is '-eer' (like engineer, career).
Add -ing: volunteer + ing.
The correct word is 'volunteering'.

review.note: The word after (36) is printed as 'or' in the scan because the first letter is missing; it is transcribed as 'for' ('volunteering for the student council project').

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++by++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong preposition).
'to be tasked **with** something' means to be given a job to do.
For example: 'The prefects were tasked with keeping the hall quiet.'
The correct word is 'with'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++enviromantle++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means to do with nature and our surroundings.
Start from the base word 'environment'. Remember the 'n' before 'ment': en-vi-ron-ment.
Add the suffix -al to make the adjective: environment + al. The ending is '-tal', not '-tle'.
The correct word is 'environmental'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++are++.

explanation: This is a grammar error with two things to fix.
Agreement: 'everyone' is singular, so it cannot take 'are'.
Tense: the story is told in the past ('The principal had also made it clear that...'), so the verb must be past: was expecting.
The correct word is 'was'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++skrold++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means moved through text or pictures on a screen.
The base word is 'scroll': the 'sk' sound is spelt 'sc' (like screen, scratch), and it ends in double 'l'.
Add -ed for the past tense: scroll + ed.
The correct word is 'scrolled'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++begin++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (verb form). Look at the helping verb in front: 'had ___'.
Rule: had + past participle makes the past perfect tense.
The verb changes like this: begin (present), began (past), begun (past participle). After 'had' we need 'begun', not 'began'.
The correct word is 'begun'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++sprauling++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word describes something that spreads out over a large area.
The 'or' sound in the middle is spelt 'aw' (like crawl, shawl): sprawl.
Add -ing: sprawl + ing.
The correct word is 'sprawling'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++Althought++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong connector), not just a spelling slip.
The word starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma, and the sentence after it is complete on its own. 'Although' cannot be used this way, because it must join two clauses in one sentence.

The sentence is a contrast with the one before: Jia Wei wanted to find out the facts, but his friends cared more about posters. The connector that starts a contrasting sentence and takes a comma is 'However'.
The correct word is 'However'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++konsept++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means an idea or plan.
Both hard and soft sounds are spelt with 'c': the first 'c' sounds like 'k' and the second sounds like 's' (con-cept).
Related words help: conception, accept, except.
The correct word is 'concept'.

review.note: The full stop after (44) is missing in the scan and has been added.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++what++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong word).
The word comes before the adverb 'easily'. To show degree before an adjective or adverb, we use 'how': how easily, how quickly, how tall.
'what' is used before a noun: what a pity, what a surprise.
The correct word is 'how'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clue: Zubir 'grew up in a poor household'. In a poor home there is too little money.
The word 'but' sets up a contrast: money was lacking, but music was always there.
'money was always not enough' gives that meaning.
The answer is 'not'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: The phrase '___ a teenager' tells us when he left home: at the time he was a teenager.
'As a teenager' means 'when he was a teenager'. Compare: 'As a child, I loved drawing.'
It starts the sentence, so use a capital letter.
The answer is 'As'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence says what he wanted to be: 'to become a professional musician'.
We need a noun for something a person strongly wants to achieve. 'from childhood' shows he had held it for a long time.
'ambition' fits. 'dream' and 'aspiration' mean the same.
The answer is 'ambition'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence describes paid work: 'playing the violin and piano in silent movie theatres'. The next sentence says 'The work was tiring and the pay was low'.
'The first ___ he had' needs a countable noun for a piece of paid work.
'work' is uncountable, so 'the first work he had' is wrong.
The answer is 'job'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'bring something to life' is a fixed phrase. It means to make something lively and exciting.
Silent movies had no sound, so the live music made the film feel alive for the audience.
The answer is 'life'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: After 'invited him to' we need a base-form verb whose object is 'a special song'.
Zubir was a composer, and the same paragraph later says 'to write the perfect song'.
'write' fits. 'compose' means the same and is also correct.
The answer is 'write'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: He was invited to do a task. What did he do with the invitation? 'readily' means willingly and without delay.
To agree to take on a task is to 'accept' it. The story is in the past tense, so: accepted.
The next sentence shows he started work on it straight away.
The answer is 'accepted'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is the subject of 'would inspire him', so it must be a pronoun.
What did he hope would inspire him? Walking along the crowded streets and quiet kampungs. 'this' points back to that whole action.
'they' (the streets and kampungs) also makes sense.
The answer is 'this'.

review.note: Open cloze: solved as 'they' (the streets and kampungs); the key gives 'this' (the walk). Both are grammatical, so the key's word is the value and 'they', 'these', 'it' and 'that' are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the pattern: He ___ the song **to capture** the aspirations of a young nation. This is verb + object + to-infinitive.
The sentence tells us his aim for the song. 'wanted the song to capture' fits the pattern and the past tense.
'hoped' is tempting, but it does not fit the pattern: we say 'hoped that the song would', not 'hoped the song to'.
The answer is 'wanted'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is the thing he 'composed', which people 'could remember and sing with pride'. It is a piece of music.
It is described as 'clear and rousing' (stirring), and the passage is about the national anthem.
'anthem' fits. 'melody', 'tune' and 'song' are also correct.
The answer is 'anthem'.

review.note: Open cloze: solved as 'melody'; the key gives 'anthem'. Both fit, so the key's word is the value and 'melody', 'tune' and similar words are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: The song 'impressed the leaders', so afterwards it was officially taken as the national anthem.
'was later ___ as' is the passive voice, so we need a past participle.
'adopted' means formally chosen and accepted. 'chosen' and 'selected' also fit.
The answer is 'adopted'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Although' signals a contrast between the two halves of the sentence.
Second half: he 'kept improving his musical technique by listening carefully to other composers'. He taught himself.
So the first half must say he did not have formal training: he never studied at prestigious music schools.
The answer is 'never'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is followed by base verbs: '___ not only **sound** grand but also **encourage** citizens'. A modal verb goes before a base verb.
The sentence gives Zubir's belief about what a national anthem ought to do. The modal for what is right or ideal is 'should'.
'must' also fits.
The answer is 'should'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'like the Primary 5 National Education (NE) Show' gives an example of the blank, so we need a plural noun for that kind of occasion.
The anthem is sung at formal national occasions.
'ceremonies' fits. 'events' and 'celebrations' are also correct. It must be plural because there is no 'a' and it is joined to 'assemblies'.
The answer is 'ceremonies'.

review.note: Open cloze: solved as 'events'; the key gives 'ceremonies'. Both fit, so the key's word is the value and 'events', 'celebrations' and 'occasions' are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: Why do students sing the anthem? 'so that they are ___ of the sacrifices and dreams that helped build Singapore'.
The word must go with 'of'. Singing the anthem brings those sacrifices back to mind: 'reminded of'.
'aware of' and 'mindful of' also fit.
The answer is 'reminded'.

questions.stem:
None of the plates in the sink is clean.
All ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: All the plates in the sink are dirty.
accept: All of the plates in the sink are dirty.

explanation: 'None ... is clean' means every single plate is not clean. Starting with 'All' turns the sentence from negative to positive, so the adjective changes to its opposite: clean becomes dirty.
Agreement: 'All the plates' is plural, so the verb changes from 'is' to 'are'.
Do not write 'All the plates in the sink are not clean'. That can also mean only some are not clean, so the meaning is no longer exact.
Answer: All the plates in the sink are dirty. ('All of the plates' is also accepted.)

review.keyAnswer: All (of) the plates in the sink are dirty.
review.solvedAnswer: All the plates in the sink are dirty.

questions.stem:
The chef works very hard, but he cannot perfect the new recipe.
However ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: However hard he works, the chef cannot perfect the new recipe.
accept: However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.

explanation: Here 'However' is not followed by a comma. The pattern is However + adjective or adverb + subject + verb, and it means 'no matter how'.
Take the adverb 'hard' and put it right after 'However'. Drop 'very' and 'but': However hard he works, ...
Put a comma, then the main clause. Make sure 'the chef' is named once so the reader knows who 'he' is.
Answer: However hard he works, the chef cannot perfect the new recipe. ('However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.' is also correct.)

review.keyAnswer: However hard he works, the chef cannot perfect the new recipe.
review.solvedAnswer: However hard the chef works, he cannot perfect the new recipe.

questions.stem:
The ice cubes are placed in the container after you break them up.
It is only ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: It is only after you break up the ice cubes that they are placed in the container.
accept: It is only after you break the ice cubes up that they are placed in the container.

explanation: The pattern is: It is only + time phrase + **that** + main clause. It stresses when something happens.
The time phrase is 'after you break them up'. It now comes first, so 'them' must be replaced by the noun: after you break up the ice cubes.
Add 'that', then the main clause, changing the noun to a pronoun: that they are placed in the container.
Keep the present tense. Answer: It is only after you break up the ice cubes that they are placed in the container.

review.keyAnswer: It is only after you break up the ice cubes / break the ice cubes up that they are placed in the container.
review.solvedAnswer: It is only after you break the ice cubes up that they are placed in the container.

questions.stem:
Father reminded Lisa, "Do your homework before meeting your friends."
Lisa was reminded ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.
accept: Lisa was reminded by her father to do her homework before meeting her friends.

explanation: Two changes are needed: active to passive, and direct speech to reported speech.
Passive: Lisa is now the subject, so the doer goes after 'by': Lisa was reminded by Father ...
A command in reported speech becomes to + base verb: 'Do your homework' becomes 'to do her homework'.
Pronouns change to fit Lisa: 'your' becomes 'her' both times. No quotation marks are needed.
Answer: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.

review.keyAnswer: Lisa was reminded by Father/her father to do her homework before meeting her friends.
review.solvedAnswer: Lisa was reminded by Father to do her homework before meeting her friends.

questions.stem:
Many were absent from swimming lessons during the rainy season.
There was high ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: There was high absenteeism from swimming lessons during the rainy season.

explanation: After the adjective 'high' we need a noun, so the adjective 'absent' must change to a noun form.
'Many were absent' is about how often or how many people stayed away. The noun for that is 'absenteeism', and it can be 'high' or 'low'.
'absence' is tempting, but we do not say 'high absence'. Check the spelling: absent + ee + ism.
Keep the rest of the sentence. Answer: There was high absenteeism from swimming lessons during the rainy season.

review.keyAnswer: There was high absenteeism from swimming lessons during the rainy season.
review.solvedAnswer: There was high absenteeism from swimming lessons during the rainy season.

questions.stem: Pick out a four-word phrase from the first paragraph which tells us that Maya's grandfather cherished the vegetable garden.

explanation: To 'cherish' something is to love it and care about it very much.
Paragraph 1: the garden 'was truly the **apple of his eye**'. This idiom means the thing a person loves most.
Count exactly four words and copy them without changing anything: apple (1) of (2) his (3) eye (4). Leave out 'the', or the phrase has five words.
The answer is 'apple of his eye'.

questions.stem: Give two reasons why Maya's mother was concerned for her when Maya asked to take care of the garden.

answer.value: Taking care of the garden would be a big responsibility, as plants need daily attention, and it would be an uphill (difficult) task for Maya.

explanation: Find Mother's reply in paragraph 2, right after 'Her mother gave her a concerned look'.
Reason 1 (1 mark): 'This would be a big responsibility, Maya. Plants need daily attention, you know?'
Reason 2 (1 mark): 'It'll be an uphill task for you.' An uphill task is a very difficult one.
Give both reasons clearly, and answer as a statement, not as Mother's question.

review.keyAnswer: Taking care of the garden was a big responsibility [1m], and it might be a difficult (/an uphill) task for Maya [1m].
review.solvedAnswer: It was a big responsibility (plants need daily attention) and it would be an uphill task for her. Agrees with key.

questions.stem:
Circle one word that best describes how Maya felt when she saw her grandfather's plants wilting. DO NOT CIRCLE MORE THAN ONE WORD.
frustrated / guilty / dismayed / anxious
(Type the word you would circle.)

explanation: Find the moment in paragraph 1: 'Maya's heart sank as she saw her dear grandfather's plants beginning to wilt'.
When your 'heart sinks', you suddenly feel sad and disappointed. 'dismayed' means upset and disappointed by something unpleasant.

'anxious' is tempting, but it means worried about what might happen; a sinking heart shows sadness. She had done nothing wrong, so she was not 'guilty', and nothing was blocking her efforts yet, so she was not 'frustrated'.
The answer is 'dismayed'.

questions.stem:
Write 1, 2 and 3 in the blanks below to indicate the order in which the events occurred in the story.
_____ Maya's grandfather fell ill and was hospitalised.
_____ Mrs Chen taught Maya how to take care of plants.
_____ Maya decided to take care of her grandfather's plants.
(Type the three numbers in the order of the blanks, from top to bottom.)

explanation: Find each event in the passage and note its paragraph.
Grandfather fell ill and stayed in hospital: paragraph 1. This is first.
Maya asked her mother if she could take care of the garden: paragraph 2. This is second.
Mrs Chen came and explained about watering: paragraphs 4 and 5. This is third.
Reading the blanks from top to bottom, the answer is 1, 3, 2.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a

answer.value: The aromatic herbs growing noticeably faster after Sandie and Maya talked to them.

explanation: Read the whole sentence: 'Sandie discovered that the aromatic herbs grew noticeably faster after they talked to them, though Maya suspected **it** was just a coincidence.'
A coincidence is two things happening together by chance. What did Maya think was only chance? The herbs growing faster after the girls talked to them.
'it' refers to a whole event, so the answer needs both halves: the herbs grew faster, and this was after Sandie and Maya talked to them. Writing only 'the herbs' is not enough.
The answer is the herbs growing faster after Sandie and Maya talked to them.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Maya sprinkling the soap solution that she had prepared onto the affected (lettuce) leaves.

explanation: Read the sentence before it: Maya 'prepared a soap solution which she sprinkled onto the affected leaves'.
Then: 'the tiny green invaders disappear completely after her **treatment**'. The treatment is what she did to get rid of the aphids.
Say what was done and to what: the soap solution sprinkled onto the affected leaves.
The answer is Maya sprinkling the soap solution onto the affected leaves.

review.keyAnswer: a) the herbs/plants growing faster after Sandie and Maya talked to them. b) Maya sprinkling the soap solution (which she had prepared) onto the affected leaves.
review.solvedAnswer: a) the herbs growing faster after the girls talked to them; b) sprinkling the soap solution onto the affected leaves. Agrees with key.
review.note: The key's own table prints 'it (line 2)'; the question paper says line 27, which is where 'it' is printed in bold.

questions.stem: Based on the information from lines 10–27 (paragraphs 3 to 6), fill in the following table. Write in complete sentences.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What Maya did when she saw the lettuce leaves look droopy

answer.value: Maya called her best friend, Sandie, for advice.

explanation: The droopy lettuce is at the end of paragraph 3. Read on to see what Maya did next.
Paragraph 4: 'Feeling extremely discouraged, Maya called her best friend, Sandie, for advice.'
The marker looks for: called Sandie, for advice. Write a complete sentence.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Sandie offered to ask her grandmother for her opinion and call Maya back immediately.

explanation: Sandie's reply is in paragraph 4: 'My grandmother grows vegetables too! Let me ask her for her opinion and I will call you back immediately.'
Turn her spoken words into a statement: she offered to ask her grandmother and to call Maya back.
The marker looks for both actions: ask her grandmother, and call Maya back.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: What Mrs Chen taught Maya about watering plants

answer.value: Mrs Chen taught Maya that different plants need different amounts of water. (For example, the soil for lettuce should not be too wet.)

explanation: Mrs Chen's lesson is in paragraph 5: 'different plants need different amount of water'.
She gave an example: 'the soil for lettuce should not be too wet'.
The marker looks for: different plants need different amounts of water.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: How Maya responded (to what Mrs Chen taught her)

answer.value: Maya took Sandie's grandmother's advice to heart, taking special care not to overwater the plants, especially the lettuce.

explanation: Look at what Maya did after the lesson, in paragraph 6.
'Maya took Sandie's grandmother's advice to heart, taking special care not to overwater the plants, especially the lettuce.'
The marker looks for the action: she took special care not to overwater the plants.

review.keyAnswer: a) Maya called her best friend Sandie for advice. b) Sandie offered to ask her grandmother and call Maya back. c) Different plants need different amounts of water. d) Maya took Sandie's grandmother's advice to heart, taking special care not to overwater the plants, especially the lettuce.
review.solvedAnswer: a) She called Sandie for advice. b) Sandie offered to ask her grandmother and call back. c) Different plants need different amounts of water. d) She took care not to overwater the plants. Agrees with key.
review.note: The fourth box is not labelled on the question paper; it is labelled (d) here, as in the key. The key heads that box 'How Maya acted on the advice' while the question paper prints 'How Maya responded'. The 4 marks are taken as 1 mark per box.

questions.stem: Explain clearly what Mrs Chen meant when she said that "Rome wasn't built in a day, and neither is a beautiful garden." (line 22, paragraph 5)

answer.value: Mrs Chen meant that it takes time and patience to grow a beautiful garden, just as the great city of Rome took a long time to build.

explanation: 'Rome wasn't built in a day' is a saying. Rome was a great city that took a very long time to build, so the saying means that good things cannot be rushed.
The clue is the sentence just before it: 'Gardening requires patience.'
Apply the saying to the garden: 'neither is a beautiful garden' means a beautiful garden also cannot be made quickly.
The marker looks for two ideas: time and patience (1 mark), and that these are needed to grow a beautiful garden (1 mark). Do not just repeat the saying.

review.keyAnswer: She meant that it takes patience / and time [1m] to grow a (beautiful) garden [1m].
review.solvedAnswer: It takes time and patience to grow a beautiful garden; it cannot be rushed. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on lines 10–32 (paragraphs 3 to 7), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Maya had no experience taking care of plants before looking after her grandfather's garden.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Maya had watched her grandfather taking care of his garden countless times but had never done it herself.

explanation: Paragraph 3: 'Although she had watched her grandfather's practised movements countless times, doing it herself the first time felt like an arduous task.'
'the first time' shows she had only watched before and had never done the work herself. She was also 'not sure how much water each plant actually needed'.
So the statement is True. The reason must be evidence from the passage, not the statement repeated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Maya solved the aphid problem with help from Sandie and Mrs Chen.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Maya solved the problem on her own: she researched natural remedies online and prepared a soap solution which she sprinkled onto the affected leaves.

explanation: Paragraph 7 describes the aphids. Look at who did the actions: '**she** researched effective natural remedies online and prepared a soap solution which **she** sprinkled onto the affected leaves'.
Sandie and Mrs Chen are not mentioned in this paragraph at all. The trap is that they did help earlier, with watering and weeding.
So the statement is False, and the reason is that Maya solved it herself by researching remedies and making the soap solution.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
Mrs Chen was encouraging when she spoke to Maya.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. She told Maya that she was doing remarkably well.

explanation: Paragraph 5: Mrs Chen's first words were 'You're doing remarkably well, dear'.
She praised Maya before correcting her, and she 'explained patiently'. Praise like this gives a person confidence, which is what 'encouraging' means.
So the statement is True, and the reason is that she told Maya she was doing remarkably well.

review.keyAnswer: a) True: Maya had watched her grandfather taking care of his garden countless times but had never done it herself. b) False: Maya solved the problem herself/on her own/independently (by looking for natural remedies online and preparing a soap solution for the treatment). c) True: She told Maya that she was doing remarkably well.
review.solvedAnswer: a) True; b) False (she researched remedies and made the soap solution herself); c) True ('You're doing remarkably well, dear'). Agrees with key.
review.note: The watermark covers parts of the key for this question (the words False and True in rows b and c, and a few words of the reasons); they are readable at high zoom and match the solved answers.

questions.stem:
Maya's grandfather told her that she had done "something wonderful" (line 35, paragraph 8).
What did Maya do that was wonderful?

answer.value: Maya had taken care of her grandfather's garden while he was in hospital, keeping all the plants healthy and thriving and making the garden more beautiful than ever.

explanation: He said this while 'pointing at the plot of land', so the wonderful thing is about the garden.
What she did (1 mark): she took care of his garden while he was in hospital.
The result (1 mark): he returned 'to find his garden more beautiful than ever' and 'saw the healthy plants'. Paragraph 7 says the garden went 'from wilting to thriving under her dedicated care'.
Give both the action and its result.

review.keyAnswer: Maya had been able to take care of her grandfather's garden while he was in hospital [1m], keeping all the plants healthy and thriving / and made it more beautiful [1m].
review.solvedAnswer: She looked after his garden while he was in hospital, so the plants were healthy and the garden was more beautiful than ever. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: How had Mother's opinion of Maya changed by the end of the story?

answer.value: At first, Mother doubted that Maya could take care of her grandfather's garden. At the end of the story, she was convinced that Maya was responsible and capable of taking care of the garden.

explanation: A 'how did it change' question needs both sides: the opinion before (1 mark) and the opinion after (1 mark).
Before (paragraph 2): Mother 'gave her a concerned look' and asked 'Are you sure you want to do it?', saying 'It'll be an uphill task for you.' She doubted that Maya could manage.
After (paragraph 10): when Grandfather asked Maya to be his gardening partner, 'Her mother nodded and gave her a thumbs-up.' She now approved and believed Maya was capable and responsible.
Use signal words such as 'At first ... At the end ...' so the marker can see the change.

review.keyAnswer: At first, she doubted/was skeptical if Maya could take care of her grandfather's garden. [1m] At the end of the story, she was convinced that Maya could take care of the garden / that Maya was responsible/capable/meticulous/committed to gardening. [1m]
review.solvedAnswer: At first she doubted Maya could cope (concerned look, 'uphill task'); by the end she was convinced Maya was capable (nodded, thumbs-up). Agrees with key.
review.note: The watermark covers a few words at the start of each line of the key for this question; the rest is readable and the meaning is clear.
